_diagnostic_finding.summary: Directional accuracy does not imply positive P&L under fixed-hold + transaction costs
_diagnostic_finding.gap_explanation: The OOS evaluation measures directional accuracy on filtered bars (|move| >= 0.25*ATR). The backtest applies a fixed 5-bar hold and $70 round-trip cost. A BUY signal that is directionally correct (price goes up) can still lose money if the move reverses before the 5-bar exit, or if the move is smaller than the $70 cost. The 66.3% directional accuracy is measured at bar-close; the backtest P&L depends on the path over 5 bars, not just the final direction.
required_actions: Optimize exit logic: use trailing stop or ATR-based exit instead of fixed 5-bar hold
Reduce round-trip cost: target OANDA XAU_USD spread + commission < $50
Add overnight financing: ~$2-8/lot/night for 5-day avg hold
Run walk-forward P&L backtest (not just accuracy) before live deployment
The 66.3% accuracy is a necessary but not sufficient condition for profitability
